I will keep my land in the winter wheat-summer maize rotation. In Quzhou County, that is still the most dependable way for me to use the full year, match the local temperature and rainfall pattern, and spread risk across two staple crops with mature local markets and mechanized operations. Because I am older, I will keep the plan simple and standardized rather than chasing too many crops. I will use improved winter wheat seed for stability and grain quality, then follow with hybrid summer maize for higher yield potential. I will rely on soil testing and moderate fertilization instead of excessive input, irrigate wheat more often because spring moisture is less reliable, and give maize fewer irrigations because it can use summer rainfall. I will use rotary tillage after harvests because it is easier and cheaper for me to manage than repeated deep ploughing, and I will keep pesticide use limited to the main disease, weed, and insect pressure windows rather than spraying routinely.
